hints.title: Duplicate Boundary Obstacle
hints.text: Finding any occurrence of target is not enough when duplicates stretch across large intervals. How can you bias the midpoint decisions toward the extreme boundaries?

hints.title: Two-Sided Monotonic Invariant
hints.text: Run two separate range reductions: one that keeps searching left even when target is matched, and a second that continues right.

hints.title: Dual Boundary Procedure
hints.text: Write a helper findBound(isFirst). When nums[mid] == target, if isFirst is true, save mid and continue searching left (right = mid - 1); otherwise save mid and continue searching right (left = mid + 1). Return [findBound(True), findBound(False)].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (0 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Two logarithmic bisections locating exact lower and upper target indices in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Expanding outward linearly from an arbitrary match degrades to O(N) on arrays of identical elements.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Reusing a single parameterised search procedure guarantees O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean boundary search without linear expansion fallbacks when target occurs frequently.

solutions.approach: Dual bisection for first and last occurrences
